### Happens without you

| In | What happens | Who | When | Leads to | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SIGNED_IN` | the verification link expires, a day on | system | your email is not verified | `SIGNED_IN` | The same as when signed out: a verification link stops working 24 hours after it was issued, by comparison with the clock, and nothing about your session changes. Ask for a new link. | never-run |
| `PENDING_VERIFICATION` | the verification link expires, a day on | system |  | `PENDING_VERIFICATION` | A verification link stops working 24 hours after it was issued. No job does this and nothing is written: every presentation compares the link's expiry with the clock. The account stays as it is, and a new link can be asked for. The test cited moves the expiry into the past and finds the link refused and the account unchanged; the 24 hours are read from the code. | test |
| `SIGNED_IN` | a refresh token already used is presented again | system | your email is verified | `ACTIVE_SIGNED_OUT` | A refresh token of your session that had already been exchanged was presented again, by you or by someone holding a copy; the server cannot tell which. That one session is ended, so you are signed out on this device, and the account's address is emailed. Your other devices stay signed in, and nothing else about the account changes. | test |
| `SIGNED_IN` | a refresh token already used is presented again | system | your email is not verified | `PENDING_VERIFICATION` | A refresh token of your session that had already been exchanged was presented again. That one session is ended, so you are signed out on this device, and the account's address is emailed. | never-run |
| `SIGNED_IN` | the refresh token expires, thirty days unused | system | your email is verified | `ACTIVE_SIGNED_OUT` | Thirty days pass without a refresh, so the session's refresh token can no longer be exchanged and you are signed out. No job does this and nothing is written: each use compares the expiry with the clock. The test cited moves the clock 31 days on and finds the session gone from the list; the thirty days are read from the code. | test |
| `SIGNED_IN` | the refresh token expires, thirty days unused | system | your email is not verified | `PENDING_VERIFICATION` | Thirty days pass without a refresh, so the session's refresh token can no longer be exchanged and you are signed out; the account is still waiting for its address to be verified. | never-run |

## The session (one sign-in, which is a refresh-token family and the access token made for it, named by the token you send)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    state "no session (no token sent, or one that names no session)" as account_session__NO_SESSION
    state "live, access token valid" as account_session__ACCESS_VALID
    state "live, access token expired" as account_session__ACCESS_EXPIRED
    state "ended (signed out, revoked, or its refresh token ran out)" as account_session__ENDED
    account_session__NO_SESSION --> account_session__ACCESS_VALID: you - sign in
    account_session__ACCESS_EXPIRED --> account_session__ACCESS_VALID: you - exchange the refresh token for a new pair
    account_session__ACCESS_VALID --> account_session__ENDED: you - 4 actions, system - a refresh token already used is presented again
    account_session__ACCESS_EXPIRED --> account_session__ENDED: you - 2 actions, system - 2 actions
    account_session__ACCESS_VALID --> account_session__ACCESS_EXPIRED: system - access token expires, fifteen minutes on
```

### Every action in every state

| Action | `NO_SESSION` | `ACCESS_VALID` | `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | `ENDED` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sign in<br>`POST /auth/login` | 200 → `ACCESS_VALID` (the sign-in is accepted (the account says when))<br>401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (the sign-in is refused) | 200 stays (the sign-in is accepted (the account says when))<br>401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (the sign-in is refused) | 200 stays (no Authorization header is sent, and the sign-in is accepted (the account says when))<br>401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (no Authorization header is sent, and the sign-in is refused)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries the expired access token) | 200 stays (no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, and the sign-in is accepted (the account says when))<br>401 `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, and the sign-in is refused)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries an access token that is no longer accepted) |
| exchange the refresh token for a new pair<br>`POST /auth/refresh` | 401 `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` | 200 stays (you send the session's current refresh token)<br>401 `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` (you send a refresh token of this session that was already exchanged for a newer one) | 200 → `ACCESS_VALID` (no Authorization header is sent, and you send the session's current refresh token)<br>401 `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` (no Authorization header is sent, and you send a refresh token of this session that was already exchanged for a newer one)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries the expired access token) | 401 `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` (no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, and the session was revoked: by logout, by being removed from the sessions list, by logout-all, by a password reset, or by an earlier reuse)<br>401 `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` (no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, the session ran out, and you send its last refresh token, now more than 30 days old)<br>401 `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` (no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, the session ran out, and you send an older refresh token of it that had been exchanged)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries an access token that is no longer accepted) |
| sign out of this session<br>`POST /auth/logout` | 204 stays (no Authorization header is sent)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header is sent whose token is not accepted) | 204 → `ENDED` | 204 → `ENDED` (no Authorization header is sent)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries the expired access token) | 204 stays (no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries an access token that is no longer accepted) |
| sign out everywhere<br>`POST /auth/logout-all` | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 204 → `ENDED` | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 204 stays (its access token is still accepted: the session ended by logout, by being removed from the sessions list or by a reuse, and the token has not yet expired (15 minutes, and the 60 seconds more the server allows))<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (its access token is no longer accepted: logout-all or a password reset ended it, or the token has expired) |
| read your profile<br>`GET /me` | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 200 stays | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 200 stays (its access token is still accepted: the session ended by logout, by being removed from the sessions list or by a reuse, and the token has not yet expired (15 minutes, and the 60 seconds more the server allows))<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (its access token is no longer accepted: logout-all or a password reset ended it, or the token has expired) |
| list your sessions<br>`GET /auth/sessions` | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 200 stays | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 200 stays (its access token is still accepted: the session ended by logout, by being removed from the sessions list or by a reuse, and the token has not yet expired (15 minutes, and the 60 seconds more the server allows))<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (its access token is no longer accepted: logout-all or a password reset ended it, or the token has expired) |
| end one session<br>`DELETE /auth/sessions/{id}` | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 204 → `ENDED` (the id is this session's)<br>204 stays (the id is another live session of yours)<br>404 `NOT_FOUND` (the id is anything else: not a UUID, somebody else's session, one that never existed, or one already ended or expired) | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 204 stays (its access token is still accepted (see GET /me in this state for when), and the id is another live session of yours)<br>404 `NOT_FOUND` (its access token is still accepted, and the id is anything else, this session's own included)<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (its access token is no longer accepted: logout-all or a password reset ended it, or the token has expired) |
| set a new password with a reset link<br>`POST /auth/reset-password` | 200 stays (no Authorization header is sent, and the reset link is live (see the password reset))<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header is sent whose token is not accepted) | 200 → `ENDED` (the reset link is live (see the password reset)) | 200 → `ENDED` (no Authorization header is sent, and the reset link is live (see the password reset))<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries the expired access token) | 200 stays (no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, and the reset link is live (see the password reset))<br>401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` (an Authorization header carries an access token that is no longer accepted) |

### You can

| In | Action | When | Leads to | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NO_SESSION` | sign in | the sign-in is accepted (the account says when) | `ACCESS_VALID` | A session begins: a new refresh-token family with its first refresh token, good for 30 days, and an access token good for 15 minutes that names the session. If the request describes a device, it is recorded for the sessions list. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | sign in | the sign-in is accepted (the account says when) | stays | Signing in again does not replace this session. The new sign-in is a session of its own, which starts with a valid access token; this one stays as it was. The probe cited signs in a second time; the list read after it shows both sessions. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | sign in | no Authorization header is sent, and the sign-in is accepted (the account says when) | stays | Signing in again does not refresh this session. The new sign-in is a session of its own, which starts with a valid access token; this one stays as it was. This one can still be refreshed, or left to run out. | never-run |
| `ENDED` | sign in | no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, and the sign-in is accepted (the account says when) | stays | An ended session is never revived. The new sign-in is a session of its own, which starts with a valid access token; this one stays as it was. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | exchange the refresh token for a new pair | you send the session's current refresh token | stays | The token is exchanged: a new access token good for 15 minutes and a new refresh token good for 30 days, in the same session. The old refresh token is marked as used and must not be sent again. Nothing requires the access token to have expired first, and the one you held before is accepted until its own 15 minutes end. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | exchange the refresh token for a new pair | no Authorization header is sent, and you send the session's current refresh token | `ACCESS_VALID` | This is the way back from an expired access token, provided the expired token is not sent along: the refresh token is exchanged for a new pair in the same session, and the sessions list shows the session as seen just now. The old refresh token is marked as used and must not be sent again. | test |
| `NO_SESSION` | sign out of this session | no Authorization header is sent | stays | The refresh token matches none on record and nothing changes. The answer is 204 all the same, so that logout cannot be used to test whether a token exists. | test |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | sign out of this session |  | `ENDED` | The session is ended: every refresh token of its family is revoked, whichever of them was sent. Logout needs no access token, and a valid one sent along changes nothing. The session's access token is not cancelled: it is accepted until its 15 minutes run out, and until then it still reads and writes. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | sign out of this session | no Authorization header is sent | `ENDED` | The session is ended: every refresh token of its family is revoked, whichever of them was sent. Logout needs no access token, so an expired one is no obstacle as long as it is not sent. | never-run |
| `ENDED` | sign out of this session | no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted | stays | Logging out twice is not an error: there is nothing left to revoke and the answer is 204 again. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | sign out everywhere |  | `ENDED` | Every session of the account ends, this one included, and the account's sign-out time is set to now, so every access token issued before this second stops being accepted on the next request. This is what logout alone does not do. The comparison is by whole seconds, so a token issued in the very second of the call survives it. | test |
| `ENDED` | sign out everywhere | its access token is still accepted: the session ended by logout, by being removed from the sessions list or by a reuse, and the token has not yet expired (15 minutes, and the 60 seconds more the server allows) | stays | The token of an ended session still proves who you are, so the call goes through: every other session of the account ends and every access token stops being accepted, this one included. The probe cited sends the access token of a session it has just logged out of. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | read your profile |  | stays | Your own profile: id, email, display name, locale, emailVerified and status. It is read from the account at each call, so it shows a verification made a moment ago without a new token. | smoke |
| `ENDED` | read your profile | its access token is still accepted: the session ended by logout, by being removed from the sessions list or by a reuse, and the token has not yet expired (15 minutes, and the 60 seconds more the server allows) | stays | Ending one session does not cancel its access token. Until its 15 minutes run out the token is accepted everywhere a token is needed, and the profile is returned as before. | never-run |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | list your sessions |  | stays | The account's live sessions, most recently seen first: for each its id, its device if one was described at sign-in, when it began, when it last refreshed, and current: true on the one this access token belongs to. No token appears in the list. | smoke |
| `ENDED` | list your sessions | its access token is still accepted: the session ended by logout, by being removed from the sessions list or by a reuse, and the token has not yet expired (15 minutes, and the 60 seconds more the server allows) | stays | The token still works, and the list it returns no longer holds this session: only the account's other live sessions, none marked current, or an empty list. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | end one session | the id is this session's | `ENDED` | Ending the session you are calling from is a logout: every refresh token of its family is revoked. The access token is not cancelled; for the rest of its 15 minutes it is accepted, and the sessions list it reads no longer holds this session. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | end one session | the id is another live session of yours | stays | That other session ends; this one is untouched and can still refresh. For the session that was named, see this same action with its own id: its refresh token is dead and its access token lives out its 15 minutes. | smoke |
| `ENDED` | end one session | its access token is still accepted (see GET /me in this state for when), and the id is another live session of yours | stays | The token of an ended session still proves who you are for the rest of its 15 minutes, so it can end another of the account's sessions. | never-run |
| `NO_SESSION` | set a new password with a reset link | no Authorization header is sent, and the reset link is live (see the password reset) | stays | There is no session to end, and resetting the password does not start one: the answer has no body and no token. Sign in with the new password afterwards. | smoke |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | set a new password with a reset link | the reset link is live (see the password reset) | `ENDED` | A password reset ends every session of the account, on every device, and sets the account's sign-out time, so this session's refresh token is dead and its access token stops being accepted at once, not after 15 minutes. | `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | set a new password with a reset link | no Authorization header is sent, and the reset link is live (see the password reset) | `ENDED` | A password reset ends every session of the account, this one included: its refresh token can no longer be exchanged. | never-run |
| `ENDED` | set a new password with a reset link | no Authorization header is sent, or one whose token is still accepted, and the reset link is live (see the password reset) | stays | The session was already over. If its access token was still being accepted, it stops being accepted now: a reset cancels every access token issued before it. | never-run |

### Happens without you

| In | What happens | Who | When | Leads to | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACCESS_VALID` | the access token expires, fifteen minutes on | system |  | `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | Fifteen minutes after it was issued the access token is refused; the server allows 60 seconds more for a clock that is wrong. No job does this: the token carries its own expiry and each request compares it with the clock. The session itself is still live and its refresh token still works. The test cited presents a token two minutes past its expiry and finds it refused; the fifteen minutes are read from the code, and a sign-in answers expiresIn 900. | test |
| `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | the refresh token expires, thirty days unused | system |  | `ENDED` | A refresh token lasts 30 days from the sign-in or refresh that issued it. Left unused that long, it can no longer be exchanged and the session is over: it leaves the sessions list and cannot be ended by id. Nothing is written and nothing is revoked; each use compares the expiry with the clock. It cannot happen while the access token is valid, since both tokens are issued together. The test cited moves the clock 31 days on; the thirty days are read from the code. | test |
| `ACCESS_VALID` | a refresh token already used is presented again | system |  | `ENDED` | A refresh token of this session that had already been exchanged is presented again, by you or by someone holding a copy. Every refresh token of the session's family is revoked, the newest included, though it was never misused, and the account's address is emailed. Only this session ends: the account's other sessions are untouched, and this session's access token is accepted until its 15 minutes run out. | test |
| `ACCESS_EXPIRED` | a refresh token already used is presented again | system |  | `ENDED` | A refresh token of this session that had already been exchanged is presented again. Every refresh token of the session's family is revoked, the newest included, and the account's address is emailed. Only this session ends. | never-run |
| `ENDED` | a refresh token already used is presented again | system | the session had run out and had not been revoked | `ENDED` | An exchanged refresh token of a session that has since run out is presented. The session was already over and stays over; its family is now marked revoked as well, and the account's address is emailed as for any reuse. A session that was revoked is different: there the token is refused as invalid and nothing more happens. | never-run |

## The password reset (one reset link, named by its token)

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    state "none (no link, or a token that matches none)" as account_reset__NONE
    state "requested, the link is live" as account_reset__REQUESTED
    state "link used" as account_reset__USED
    state "link expired" as account_reset__EXPIRED
    account_reset__NONE --> account_reset__REQUESTED: you - ask for a password reset link
    account_reset__REQUESTED --> account_reset__USED: you - set a new password with a reset link
    account_reset__REQUESTED --> account_reset__EXPIRED: system - reset link expires, an hour on
```

### Every action in every state

| Action | `NONE` | `REQUESTED` | `USED` | `EXPIRED` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ask for a password reset link<br>`POST /auth/forgot-password` | 202 → `REQUESTED` (an account has this address, verified or not)<br>202 stays (no account has this address) | 202 stays | 202 stays | 202 stays |
| set a new password with a reset link<br>`POST /auth/reset-password` | 422 `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_INVALID` | 200 → `USED` | 410 `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED` | 410 `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED` |

### You can

| In | Action | When | Leads to | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NONE` | ask for a password reset link | an account has this address, verified or not | `REQUESTED` | A reset link good for one hour is made and emailed to the address. The answer is 202 with an empty body. An account that has not verified its address gets one too, since it may sign in. | test |
| `NONE` | ask for a password reset link | no account has this address | stays | Nothing is emailed. The answer is 202, as it is for an address that has an account, so the caller is not told which it was. The test cited asserts the 202 and that no email goes out; that both answers have no body is read from the controller, which returns nothing. | test |
| `REQUESTED` | ask for a password reset link |  | stays | Asking again makes a second link and emails it. This one is not cancelled: each link stays usable until its own hour ends. | never-run |
| `USED` | ask for a password reset link |  | stays | A new link is made and emailed; the used one stays used. The test cited resets twice, each time through a link it asked for. | test |
| `EXPIRED` | ask for a password reset link |  | stays | A new link is made and emailed; the expired one stays expired. | never-run |
| `REQUESTED` | set a new password with a reset link |  | `USED` | The link is spent and the password replaced. In the same transaction any lockout is cleared, every session of the account is ended and every access token stops being accepted; afterwards the address is emailed that the password changed. The account's other live reset links are not cancelled and stay usable until their own hour ends. The new password is checked before the link is looked at, so a refused password does not spend it. | test |

### Refused here

| In | Action | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NONE` | set a new password with a reset link |  | 422 `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_INVALID` | The token matches no reset link: mistyped, cut short, never issued, or a verification link, which is looked up separately. (a test asserts the 422 for a verification link sent here, not the code) | FR-004, ADR-0022 §1 | never-run |
| `USED` | set a new password with a reset link |  | 410 `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED` | A reset link works once. Used and expired get the same answer; ask for a new link. | FR-004, ADR-0022 §1 | smoke |
| `EXPIRED` | set a new password with a reset link |  | 410 `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED` | The link's hour has passed. Nothing changes; ask for a new link. | FR-004, ADR-0022 §1 | never-run |

### Happens without you

| In | What happens | Who | When | Leads to | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `REQUESTED` | the reset link expires, an hour on | system |  | `EXPIRED` | A reset link stops working one hour after it was issued. No job does this and nothing is written: each presentation compares the link's expiry with the clock. | never-run |

## Where the contract is silent

The code answers these and `contracts/openapi.json` does not document them.

| Endpoint | Status | What the code does |

| `POST /auth/register` | 401 | 401 UNAUTHENTICATED when an Authorization header is sent whose token is not accepted: the route is public, but the resource server checks any bearer token before the controller runs. Read from the code; nothing runs it. The contract's generator gives a public auth route no 401. |
